planted.description: The image runs as root (no USER) and turns the Chrome sandbox off with PUPPETEER_DANGEROUS_NO_SANDBOX. A renderer exploit then runs code in the container. Run as a non-root user (USER $APP_UID) with the sandbox on. Docker's default seccomp profile blocks the sandbox: allow clone, clone3 and unshare in a seccomp profile, not --no-sandbox or SYS_ADMIN (SEC-24).

BrowserFetcher().DownloadAsync() when the singleton is created: each container downloads Chrome at runtime (network, disk, no pinned build, slow start). Install chrome-headless-shell at image build time, pinned to Chrome.DefaultBuildId, and set ExecutablePath or PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH.

A new browser for each render (await using var browser = await Puppeteer.LaunchAsync) and no limit on concurrent renders. Each launch costs 1 to 2 seconds and a process tree; parallel requests can exhaust memory. Keep one browser per process, a context and a page per render, and a SemaphoreSlim limit.
The customer note (free text from the webshop) is concatenated into the HTML without encoding. With JavaScript on and the network open, an , ,

GET /invoices/render?url= passes any URL to GoToAsync: a caller can render internal services, the cloud metadata endpoint, or file:// paths into a PDF (SSRF and file read). Remove the endpoint, or allow only a fixed list of hosts over https and require authorization.
PdfAsync to a temp file, then ReadAllBytesAsync and Delete: extra disk I/O and a file left behind when the process stops. Use PdfDataAsync (or PdfStreamAsync).

SetContentAsync with NavigationOptions and Networkidle0 is obsolete (CS0618: networkidle never worked reliably with SetContent), so the build with -warnaserror fails. There is no timeout and the CancellationToken is ignored. Use SetContentAsync(html, new SetContentOptions { Timeout = ... }) and set PdfOptions.Timeout.
No fonts (fonts-liberation, fonts-noto-core) and no init process (tini or docker run --init): text renders with fallback glyphs or boxes, and Chrome child processes become zombies.
